fact: The article states that after the Diamniadio National Datacenter opened in June 2021, President Macky Sall instructed his government to migrate all state data and digital platforms to it and to repatriate all national data hosted outside Senegal, and that Senegal requires servers to be housed within its borders; the author cites secondary sources and gives no legal instrument.
system: Presidential instruction to host state data in the Diamniadio National Datacenter

fact: Senegal's Presidency confirmed a proposed Cybastion partnership, with $300 million to be mobilised and financing not finalised, that includes a planned sovereign data center to host and manage critical digital systems within Senegal's borders.

Seneweb reports the National Assembly unanimously adopted bill n° 25/2026, which enshrines the principle of keeping data considered sensitive for the State on national territory (127 votes in favour, none against).

The health ministry and the state company SENUM signed a framework convention under which SENUM is to host the ministry's application data, notably the shared patient file and DHIS2 data moved from LINODE, in the national data centre.

Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko said cloud solutions are being deployed in the national data centres with security, compliance and sovereignty guarantees, and that the most sensitive data will be hosted on national territory under state control.

Senegal's ministry said a drafting workshop opened in Dakar on 20 June 2024 for a data and data-security framework law, ordered by the President on 17 April 2024 in line with its digital sovereignty policy.
system: loi d'orientation sur les données et leur sécurisation

fact: Ousmane Bop, manager of the Diamniadio national data centre, says Senegal intends to repatriate public data, of which 10 to 20 per cent is still held abroad, with options of paying off ten-year hosting contracts early or waiting for expiry, and legal solutions under study.
Le Marche finance reports that the government launched a sovereign cloud on 24 March 2026, aimed at secure hosting of public data, as part of the New Deal technologique.

La Tribune Afrique says the New Deal technologique, the national digital strategy launched in 2025, provides for developing sovereign digital infrastructure including data centres and cloud platforms.
SenePlus reports that on 4 November 2026 the Digital and Health ministries said they are jointly setting up an infrastructure to secure and host patients' health data, with no timetable given.
MFWA says a policy in force since 2021 requires state agencies to transfer the data they hold to the national Diamniadio data centre.
MFWA says state agencies have been moving their data to the Diamniadio national storage centre since November 2023, the health ministry reportedly over 80% of its data by January 2024.
